message.content:
The most recent estimates put the United States’ Gini coefficient at roughly **0.41** (or 41 %) for the year 2021–2022.  
This figure comes from the OECD’s “Income Distribution Database” and the World Bank’s “World Development Indicators.” It represents the level of income inequality among households in the U.S. and is calculated using the Lorenz curve method.  

> **Key points**  
> • A Gini coefficient of 0 indicates perfect equality; 1 indicates maximal inequality.  
> • The U.S. has been hovering around 0.40–0.42 for the past decade, slightly higher than many European peers but lower than some emerging economies.  
> • The figure is based on household income data and may vary slightly depending on the source (OECD vs. World Bank) and the exact year of measurement.  

If you need the most current year‑by‑year breakdown or a comparison with other countries, let me know!
